solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The following works mostly useless needing revision without question

indicators.note: something needing revision must be reworked, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses some later works as largely worthless and in need of rewriting, no question about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last S of USELESS to leave USELES; with Q added, 'needing revision' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sequels are books or films that follow on from earlier ones, so they are literally the following works.

clue.text: Fuel reservoir having problem with pressure

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A fuel tank has a pressure fault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is the reservoir of oil at the bottom of an engine.

clue.text: What of Caesar, breaking laws and profiting?

parts.note: quid is Latin for what, Caesar's language
to sin is to break moral laws

explanation.surface: A question about Caesar breaking the law and getting rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Quids in is a British idiom; a quid is a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quids in is British slang for being in profit, ahead financially.

clue.text: Call up in time before collecting in order

indicators.note: collecting means the time word gathers the other letters inside it

parts.note: eve is the time just before an event
OK means in order, all right

explanation.surface: A summons comes in time, before the orderly gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon up a memory or feeling, bringing it to mind.

clue.text: Associate team with what footballers do

parts.note: a side is a team
footballers kick the ball

explanation.surface: A player teams up with what footballers do.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a close companion or partner, an associate who assists.

clue.text: Noise comes on, banging at first on my inner ear

indicators.note: on here means placed after, so the exclamation comes first and the initials follow it

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a loud banging sound striking the inner ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner ear' looks anatomical, but it means the woody core of an ear of maize.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncob is the central woody part of an ear of maize, the inside of that sort of ear.

clue.text: Taking heart from band of conscientious objectors?

indicators.note: of links the group to its members, with the abbreviation written first

parts.note: CO is short for conscientious objector
a ring is a band, as of people

explanation.surface: Pacifists draw courage from their own group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking heart' suggests encouragement; it means removing the core of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Coring an apple removes its central part, literally taking the heart out of it.

clue.text: Show over, wine is quietly put down

parts.note: red is red wine
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to lay is to put down

explanation.surface: When the show ends, the wine is quietly set down.
explanation.definitionFit: To redisplay is to exhibit again, showing something over once more.

clue.text: One given time to study volume caught opening it

parts.note: to con is to study

indicators.note: opening means the catch letter splits the little word apart

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A student given time to read a book finds it gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given time' sounds like a deadline; here it is a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict is someone sentenced to a term in prison, given time.

clue.text: Lacking detail of brief collision south of minor road

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means placed below, so after

parts.note: a B road is a minor road in Britain
a brush is a brief contact

explanation.surface: A short crash is reported vaguely below a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: A B road is a British minor road, below an A road.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad-brush approach is general and sweeping, without fine detail.

clue.text: Old woman, one peer and monarch to be sent for

parts.note: old woman is slang for one's mother, MA
I is the Roman numeral one
a lord is a peer of the realm
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: An old lady, a nobleman and the sovereign are all summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail-order goods are ordered by post and dispatched to the buyer, so they are things to be sent for.

clue.text: Pass notes for couple to hold

indicators.note: to hold means the pair word keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: a duo is a couple
N is an abbreviation for note, so two notes give NN

explanation.surface: A pair keep some banknotes as they go past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' is what a quiz contestant says when stumped, and the casual 'dunno' says the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'pass' in a quiz is the same as admitting ignorance, colloquially 'I don't know'.

clue.text: Within bounds of seminars, summit, I tend to be frank

indicators.note: within means the next pieces sit inside the outer letters
the bounds of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a peak is a summit
I, the personal pronoun, can be read as one
to mind is to tend or look after

explanation.surface: Someone at a summit meeting, between seminars, admits a tendency to speak bluntly.
explanation.definitionFit: To be frank is to say openly what you think, an idiom for honest plain speaking.

clue.text: Sue chemist for falsifying papers with notes

indicators.note: falsifying means altering the letters to make something new

explanation.surface: Take a chemist to court for forging documents with notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet music is printed paper bearing musical notation, papers carrying notes.

clue.text: Awfully kind chap to single out specially

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A very kind man is chosen for special recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: To hand-pick is to select personally and carefully, choosing someone or something for special treatment.

clue.text: Crowded round antique that's turned up, protected from theft?

indicators.note: round means the crowded word goes around the other letters

parts.note: packed means crowded

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means written backwards upward

parts.note: old means antique

explanation.surface: People crowd round an antique on show, worried it will be stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Something padlocked is secured with a lock, guarding it from being stolen.

clue.text: Instrument-maker's gamble, first time out?

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, and the first of the two such letters is taken out

parts.note: a flutter is a small bet, a gamble

explanation.surface: An instrument-maker places a bet, perhaps the first time ever.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. The flutter has two Ts; only the first goes, leaving FLUTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluter is someone who makes flutes, or grooves; a rare word for a maker of that woodwind.

clue.text: Toast with a particular taste — could there be alcohol in it?

definitions.text: could there be alcohol in it?

parts.note: to brown is to toast
one's bag is one's taste or liking

explanation.surface: A toast with a distinctive flavour, perhaps a boozy one.
explanation.walkthrough: A paper bag hides a bottle for drinking in public.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown paper bag is classically used to conceal a bottle of drink, so it may hold alcohol.

clue.text: Officer in the first place briefly to turn to Morse?

indicators.note: in means the officer goes inside the shortened place
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Eden, the garden of Genesis, was the first place
NCO is a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: An officer briefly decides at once to switch to Morse code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse' might suggest Inspector Morse; here it is the dot-dash code.
explanation.definitionFit: Converting a message to Morse puts it into code, which is what encoding means.

clue.text: An element still keeping chin up, periodically

indicators.note: keeping means the calm word holds the picked letters

parts.note: calm means still

indicators.note: periodically means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: An element of composure: staying still and keeping one's chin up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' also nods to the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium is a chemical element, number 20 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Fliers you put back amidst angry noises

indicators.note: amidst means the reversed word sits in the middle of the noises

parts.note: growls are angry noises

indicators.note: put back means the word is written backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Birds are driven off with snarls.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey owls are a kind of owl, birds that fly, so they are fliers.

clue.text: Journey from Mull just being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out, so the letters follow the sound

parts.note: to mull is to weigh up; just means fair

explanation.surface: A trip to the Scottish island of Mull, as broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull looks like the Scottish island but is the verb, to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: Wayfare is an old word for travelling, a journey on foot.

clue.text: Making one fetch up quote, the writer reflected

indicators.note: reflected means seen in a mirror, so written backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote
the writer means the setter, me

explanation.surface: A writer reflects on a quote that makes someone vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic substance causes vomiting, making one fetch up one's food.

clue.text: Town memorably mistaken for one in the Midlands

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters are taken wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A town is famously confused with a Midlands one.
explanation.walkthrough: MELTON MOWBRAY is a market town in Leicestershire, in the English Midlands, famous for pork pies.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition reads 'one' as a town, and this place is a town in the Midlands.

clue.text: Europeans denied their capital stinks

indicators.note: denied their capital means losing the first letter

parts.note: Greeks are Europeans

explanation.surface: Europeans refused their capital city find it smelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeks means smells strongly and unpleasantly, so stinks.

clue.text: Colour used for filling in quite a lot

indicators.note: filling in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A paint used to fill in a large area.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal is a dark greenish-blue shade.

clue.text: Say nothing, and ruffle feathers of duck

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
to ruffle someone's feathers is to irk them

explanation.surface: Keep quiet and disturb the plumage of a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' looks like the bird, given the feathers, but it is the verb meaning to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a duty is to avoid it, the same as to shirk it.

clue.text: I'm obliged to exercise caution when handling large knives etc

parts.note: ta is a British way of saying thanks, I'm obliged

indicators.note: handling means holding, so the caution word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: beware means exercise caution

explanation.surface: A grateful person promises to be careful with big knives and other kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tableware covers the cutlery, plates and dishes used at meals, of which knives are examples.

clue.text: Funny fellow sharing practice?

definitions.meaning: funny here means amusing, as in a comic performance
split as ..., a fellow doctor sharing a medical practice

explanation.surface: An amusing partner in a medical practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedic means comic or amusing; read as co-medic it is a partner doctor.

clue.text: Novelist's chat with Australian outlaw cut short

parts.note: to gas is to chat idly

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Ned Kelly was the famous Australian outlaw

explanation.surface: A novelist talks with a bushranger who is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell was a Victorian English author of Cranford and North and South.
